# Setup and Data Loading

This document contains the technical analyses needed for the model card: SHAP explainability, fairness analysis, and decision threshold optimization.

```{python}
# Import required libraries
import polars as pl
import polars.selectors as cs
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pickle
from plotnine import *

# Machine learning
from sklearn.metrics import (
    accuracy_score, 
    roc_auc_score, 
    confusion_matrix, 
    classification_report,
    roc_curve,
    precision_recall_curve
)

# Set display options
pl.Config.set_tbl_rows(10)
```

```{python}
# Load the enhanced training data
df_train = pl.read_csv(
    "application_train_fully_imputed.csv",
    infer_schema_length=None
)

print(f"Training data shape: {df_train.shape}")
print(f"Total samples: {df_train.height:,}")
```

```{python}
# Prepare data (same as modeling notebook)
feature_cols = [col for col in df_train.columns if col not in ["SK_ID_CURR", "TARGET"]]

X = df_train.select(feature_cols)
y = df_train.get_column("TARGET").to_numpy()

# One-hot encode categorical variables
cat_cols = [col for col in X.columns if X[col].dtype == pl.Utf8]
X_pd = X.to_pandas()
X_encoded = pd.get_dummies(X_pd, columns=cat_cols, drop_first=True)

print(f"Features after encoding: {X_encoded.shape[1]}")
```

```{python}
# Train/Val split (same random_state as modeling)
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

X_train, X_val, y_train, y_val = train_test_split(
    X_encoded, 
    y, 
    test_size=0.2, 
    random_state=42,
    stratify=y
)

print(f"Training set: {X_train.shape[0]:,} samples")
print(f"Validation set: {X_val.shape[0]:,} samples")
```

```{python}
# Load the saved enhanced model
with open('rf_model_enhanced.pkl', 'rb') as f:
    rf_model = pickle.load(f)

print("✅ Model loaded successfully")
print(f"Model type: {type(rf_model).__name__}")
print(f"Number of features: {len(rf_model.feature_names_in_)}")
```

# SHAP Explainability Analysis

SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values help us understand which features drive model predictions and by how much.

```{python}
# Install shap if needed
import subprocess
import sys

try:
    import shap
    print("✅ SHAP already installed")
except ImportError:
    print("Installing SHAP...")
    subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "shap", "--quiet"])
    import shap
    print("✅ SHAP installed successfully")
```

```{python}
# Take a 1000-row sample for SHAP analysis (for speed)
np.random.seed(42)
sample_idx = np.random.choice(len(X_val), size=1000, replace=False)
X_sample = X_val.iloc[sample_idx]
y_sample = y_val[sample_idx]

print(f"SHAP sample size: {len(X_sample):,} rows")
print(f"Sample default rate: {y_sample.mean()*100:.2f}%")
```

```{python}
# Create SHAP explainer (TreeExplainer for Random Forest)
print("Creating SHAP explainer...")
explainer = shap.TreeExplainer(rf_model)

print("Calculating SHAP values for 1,000 samples...")
print("(This may take a few minutes...)")
shap_values = explainer.shap_values(X_sample)

print("✅ SHAP values calculated")
```

```{python}
# SHAP values come as [class 0, class 1] - we want class 1 (default)
shap_values_default = shap_values[1]

print(f"SHAP values shape: {shap_values_default.shape}")
print(f"Features: {shap_values_default.shape[1]}")
```

## SHAP Summary Plot

```{python}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8

# Create SHAP summary plot
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 8))
shap.summary_plot(
    shap_values_default, 
    X_sample,
    plot_type="dot",
    show=False,
    max_display=20
)
plt.title("SHAP Feature Importance - Top 20 Features", fontsize=14, pad=20)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Top 20 Most Important Features

```{python}
# Calculate mean absolute SHAP values for each feature
mean_abs_shap = np.abs(shap_values_default).mean(axis=0)

# Create DataFrame with feature importance
shap_importance = pd.DataFrame({
    'feature': X_sample.columns,
    'mean_abs_shap': mean_abs_shap
}).sort_values('mean_abs_shap', ascending=False)

# Display top 20
top_20_shap = shap_importance.head(20).reset_index(drop=True)
top_20_shap.index = top_20_shap.index + 1
top_20_shap.index.name = 'Rank'

print("\nTop 20 Most Important Features (by Mean |SHAP|):")
print(top_20_shap.to_string())
```

## SHAP Feature Importance Visualization

```{python}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8

# Plot top 20 features
(
    ggplot(top_20_shap.reset_index(), aes(x='reorder(feature, mean_abs_shap)', y='mean_abs_shap'))
    + geom_col(fill='steelblue')
    + coord_flip()
    + labs(
        title='Top 20 Most Impactful Features (SHAP Analysis)',
        x='Feature',
        y='Mean Absolute SHAP Value',
        subtitle='Higher values indicate greater impact on model predictions'
    )
    + theme_minimal()
    + theme(figure_size=(10, 8))
)
```

# Fairness Analysis

Analyzing model predictions across demographic groups to identify potential disparities.

```{python}
# Make predictions on validation set
y_pred_val = rf_model.predict(X_val)
y_prob_val = rf_model.predict_proba(X_val)[:, 1]

# Get original data with demographics
df_val = df_train.filter(
    pl.col("SK_ID_CURR").is_in(
        df_train.select("SK_ID_CURR").to_series()[X_val.index]
    )
)

# Add predictions to validation data
df_val_analysis = df_val.with_columns([
    pl.Series("predicted_default", y_pred_val),
    pl.Series("default_probability", y_prob_val)
])

print(f"Validation data with predictions: {df_val_analysis.shape}")
```

## Fairness by Gender

```{python}
# Analyze approval rates by gender
fairness_gender = (
    df_val_analysis
    .group_by("CODE_GENDER")
    .agg([
        pl.len().alias("count"),
        pl.col("predicted_default").mean().alias("predicted_default_rate"),
        pl.col("TARGET").mean().alias("actual_default_rate"),
        (1 - pl.col("predicted_default")).mean().alias("approval_rate")
    ])
    .sort("CODE_GENDER")
)

print("\nFairness Analysis by Gender:")
print(fairness_gender)
```

```{python}
# Calculate disparate impact ratio (80% rule)
approval_rates = fairness_gender.to_pandas()
if len(approval_rates) >= 2:
    max_approval = approval_rates['approval_rate'].max()
    min_approval = approval_rates['approval_rate'].min()
    disparate_impact_ratio = min_approval / max_approval
    
    print(f"\nDisparate Impact Analysis:")
    print(f"  Highest approval rate: {max_approval*100:.2f}%")
    print(f"  Lowest approval rate: {min_approval*100:.2f}%")
    print(f"  Disparate Impact Ratio: {disparate_impact_ratio:.3f}")
    print(f"  Passes 80% rule: {'✅ Yes' if disparate_impact_ratio >= 0.8 else '❌ No'}")
```

## Fairness by Education Level

```{python}
# Analyze approval rates by education
fairness_education = (
    df_val_analysis
    .group_by("NAME_EDUCATION_TYPE")
    .agg([
        pl.len().alias("count"),
        pl.col("predicted_default").mean().alias("predicted_default_rate"),
        pl.col("TARGET").mean().alias("actual_default_rate"),
        (1 - pl.col("predicted_default")).mean().alias("approval_rate")
    ])
    .sort("approval_rate")
)

print("\nFairness Analysis by Education Level:")
print(fairness_education)
```

```{python}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6

# Visualize approval rates by education
edu_df = fairness_education.to_pandas()

(
    ggplot(edu_df, aes(x='reorder(NAME_EDUCATION_TYPE, approval_rate)', y='approval_rate'))
    + geom_col(fill='steelblue')
    + geom_hline(yintercept=0.8, linetype='dashed', color='red', alpha=0.5)
    + coord_flip()
    + labs(
        title='Approval Rates by Education Level',
        x='Education Level',
        y='Approval Rate',
        subtitle='Red line shows 80% threshold for disparate impact analysis'
    )
    + scale_y_continuous(labels=lambda l: [f'{int(x*100)}%' for x in l])
    + theme_minimal()
    + theme(figure_size=(12, 6))
)
```

# Decision Threshold Analysis

Finding the optimal probability threshold based on realistic lending economics.

## Lending Economics Assumptions

Based on consumer lending industry research, we'll use realistic cost assumptions:

```{python}
# Cost assumptions (based on industry research)
# Source: Federal Reserve Bank studies on consumer lending
avg_loan_amount = df_train.select("AMT_CREDIT").mean()[0, 0]
avg_loan_term_days = df_train.select("DAYS_CREDIT").mean()[0, 0] if "DAYS_CREDIT" in df_train.columns else 365 * 3

print("Lending Economics Assumptions:")
print("=" * 70)
print(f"Average loan amount: ${avg_loan_amount:,.0f}")
print(f"\nProfit on repaid loan:")
print(f"  • Interest rate: 15% APR (typical for consumer loans)")
print(f"  • Operating costs: 3% of loan amount")
print(f"  • Net profit per repaid loan: ~12% of loan amount")
profit_per_repaid = avg_loan_amount * 0.12
print(f"  • Estimated profit: ${profit_per_repaid:,.0f}")

print(f"\nLoss on defaulted loan:")
print(f"  • Loss Given Default (LGD): 75% (industry standard)")
print(f"  • Recovery rate: 25%")
loss_per_default = avg_loan_amount * 0.75
print(f"  • Estimated loss: ${loss_per_default:,.0f}")

print(f"\nCost ratio: Loss/Profit = {loss_per_default/profit_per_repaid:.1f}:1")
print("=" * 70)
```

## Threshold Optimization

```{python}
# Calculate expected value at different thresholds
thresholds_to_test = np.arange(0.05, 0.96, 0.05)

results = []
for threshold in thresholds_to_test:
    # Make predictions at this threshold
    predictions = (y_prob_val >= threshold).astype(int)
    
    # Confusion matrix
    tn, fp, fn, tp = confusion_matrix(y_val, predictions).ravel()
    
    # Financial outcomes
    # True Negatives: Correctly approved (will repay) -> profit
    # False Positives: Incorrectly denied (would have repaid) -> opportunity cost
    # False Negatives: Incorrectly approved (will default) -> loss
    # True Positives: Correctly denied (would default) -> avoided loss
    
    approved = tn + fn  # Approved loans
    total_profit = tn * profit_per_repaid  # Profit from good loans
    total_loss = fn * loss_per_default     # Loss from bad loans
    net_value = total_profit - total_loss
    
    # Metrics
    approval_rate = (tn + fn) / len(y_val)
    default_rate_approved = fn / (tn + fn) if (tn + fn) > 0 else 0
    
    results.append({
        'threshold': threshold,
        'approval_rate': approval_rate,
        'approved_count': approved,
        'defaults_approved': fn,
        'defaults_caught': tp,
        'default_rate_approved': default_rate_approved,
        'total_profit': total_profit,
        'total_loss': total_loss,
        'net_value': net_value,
        'net_value_per_loan': net_value / len(y_val)
    })

results_df = pd.DataFrame(results)

# Find optimal threshold
optimal_idx = results_df['net_value'].idxmax()
optimal_threshold = results_df.loc[optimal_idx, 'threshold']

print(f"\nOptimal Threshold Analysis:")
print(f"Optimal threshold: {optimal_threshold:.2f}")
print(f"\nAt optimal threshold:")
print(f"  • Approval rate: {results_df.loc[optimal_idx, 'approval_rate']*100:.1f}%")
print(f"  • Default rate (among approved): {results_df.loc[optimal_idx, 'default_rate_approved']*100:.2f}%")
print(f"  • Net value: ${results_df.loc[optimal_idx, 'net_value']:,.0f}")
print(f"  • Net value per loan: ${results_df.loc[optimal_idx, 'net_value_per_loan']:,.0f}")
```

## Sensitivity Analysis

```{python}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 8

# Create visualizations
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(12, 8))

# Plot 1: Net Value vs Threshold
axes[0, 0].plot(results_df['threshold'], results_df['net_value'] / 1e6, linewidth=2)
axes[0, 0].axvline(optimal_threshold, color='red', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('Probability Threshold')
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('Net Value ($M)')
axes[0, 0].set_title('Net Value vs Decision Threshold')
axes[0, 0].grid(alpha=0.3)

# Plot 2: Approval Rate vs Threshold
axes[0, 1].plot(results_df['threshold'], results_df['approval_rate'] * 100, linewidth=2, color='green')
axes[0, 1].axvline(optimal_threshold, color='red', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)
axes[0, 1].set_xlabel('Probability Threshold')
axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('Approval Rate (%)')
axes[0, 1].set_title('Approval Rate vs Decision Threshold')
axes[0, 1].grid(alpha=0.3)

# Plot 3: Default Rate Among Approved
axes[1, 0].plot(results_df['threshold'], results_df['default_rate_approved'] * 100, linewidth=2, color='orange')
axes[1, 0].axvline(optimal_threshold, color='red', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)
axes[1, 0].set_xlabel('Probability Threshold')
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel('Default Rate (%)')
axes[1, 0].set_title('Default Rate Among Approved Loans')
axes[1, 0].grid(alpha=0.3)

# Plot 4: Profit vs Loss
axes[1, 1].plot(results_df['threshold'], results_df['total_profit'] / 1e6, 
                linewidth=2, label='Total Profit', color='green')
axes[1, 1].plot(results_df['threshold'], results_df['total_loss'] / 1e6, 
                linewidth=2, label='Total Loss', color='red')
axes[1, 1].axvline(optimal_threshold, color='red', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)
axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('Probability Threshold')
axes[1, 1].set_ylabel('Amount ($M)')
axes[1, 1].set_title('Profit vs Loss by Threshold')
axes[1, 1].legend()
axes[1, 1].grid(alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
